# osauer.dev · Software for a clearer portfolio

Updated: 2026-10-06

Personal software by Oliver Sauer: markets, applied AI and Go systems. The site
shows independent projects. It is not investment advice and makes no claim of
investment performance. Public screenshots use synthetic simulation data.

- [Canary Desk](https://osauer.dev/desk/): A portfolio workspace, in private
  preview. Written briefs, an AI analyst, risk rules and
  statement-backed FX contribution for Day, WTD, MTD and YTD. Its cash-sweep
  planner considers same-currency bills after commitments and liquidity
  reserves; it is off by default and requires owner commissioning, calibrated
  policy and current native settlement evidence.
  Opportunities, new with Canary v3.17, watches up to 20 owner-chosen stocks for unusual
  volume followed by a price that holds or rises. It shows a dated quote for an
  exact listed call before the owner sets a limit and records Worth a look /
  Skip marks, including quiet days. After eligible Canary-placed fills it
  reviews entry timing (price diagnostics before fees, not realised profit).
  Research, also new, compares dated borrowing costs and
  FINRA-reported short interest; borrowing fees are a borrower cost, not
  lending income.
  Order authority is separate from analysis. Orders need owner confirmation or
  explicitly scoped prior authority, and Canary's execution gates apply. The AI
  analyst remains read-only. Access is arranged personally; there is no
  commercial service or public Desk installer.
- [Canary CLI](https://osauer.dev/canary/): Desk's open-source broker engine,
  written in Go. It includes a native TWS protocol implementation, a daemon, the
  CLI, read-only MCP tools and a paired app. Standard downloads and all MCP
  tools cannot place orders.
  Latest release: v3.18.1 (6 October 2026). Upgrades need no policy step: when
  it starts, the daemon backs up each policy file it changes and writes the keys
  a release adds. It also fixes protection proposals that stopped refreshing in
  v3.18.0. v3.18.0 (6 October 2026) added: `canary policy show --explain` prints
  every limit, policy and runtime setting in force with its source and meaning,
  and `canary policy check` reads the config and the policy files against each
  other and, through the daemon, against the live account (`--offline` checks
  the files alone), naming each implausible value with a reason and, where one
  applies, a suggested fix. MCP clients get the same read-only report from
  `canary_policy_check`, which never changes a limit. The per-order value cap
  now scales with net liquidation value between a floor and ceiling in the
  policy file. The cash sweep's reserve follows net liquidation value and
  planned needs, bill purchases keep to a minimum and a maximum size and bill
  buys wait while any currency is borrowed. In trading builds a protective stop
  guard writes to the broker on its own, but only to shrink or cancel stop
  orders Canary itself placed; stops placed by hand are never changed.
  v3.17.0 (4 October 2026) added a durable watchlist of up
  to 20 US stocks, read-only volume-turn setup observations, a dated quote for
  an exact selected call, setup coverage and entry markouts through the CLI
  (no MCP setup tools), plus borrowing-rate, lending-screen and FINRA
  short-interest research through the CLI and read-only MCP. Setup parameters
  are observations, not validated signals; markouts exclude commissions and
  never replace account P&L. Borrowing fees are a borrower cost, not lender
  yield. v3.16.1 keeps status and MCP requests responsive while the broker is
  slow, and an explicit `canary stop` stays in force until `canary restart`.
  Since v3.16.0, cash-sweep plans show bill order
  minimums, fee bounds and advisory net gain after spread, fees and forgone
  cash interest, with an audited currency-priority preference.
  FX contribution is available in Canary v3.16.0 and in Desk's private runtime.
  `canary reporting fx --json` and `canary_reporting_fx` expose statement-day
  currency valuation contribution, separately from realised Forex lot P&L.
  Incomplete periods disclose gaps and omit a total.
- Lending observations are available in Canary v3.16.0. Dated stock loans
  appear in position evidence; `canary lending fees --json` and
  `canary_lending_fees` expose bounded earned customer net-fee history. The
  Canary app adds position annotations and expandable fees, and Desk's AI
  analyst can read the evidence. Coverage distinguishes missing history,
  partial history and a complete zero. Participation remains with Interactive
  Brokers (IBKR). Fees are kept separate from account P&L; payment and P&L
  linkage remain unproved. Populated account evidence is still needed for
  commissioning. Use v3.16.0 or later for these reporting features.
- [HyperServe](https://osauer.dev/hyperserve/): An open-source Go HTTP server
  library built on net/http, with optional MCP.
- [Torok](https://osauer.dev/torok/): The private Go agent runtime behind Canary
  Desk's morning briefs and AI analyst. It saves a run's progress as it goes.
- [Tower](https://osauer.dev/tower/): A private experiment in coordinating coding
  agents, switched off since 29 September 2026. No public download.

Use the Canary handbook for operational details and signed releases for binary
availability. Current source, the private installed runtime and the public
release are separate kinds of evidence. Desk, Torok and Tower remain private.

Public screenshot tour: weekly FX contribution, a current decision and
Opportunities. Opportunities shows synthetic five-minute price and
volume observations; a pattern match is not a proven edge or order authority.
Images were refreshed on 4 October 2026 from an isolated synthetic Desk build.
